claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively homogeneous elemental distribution.
Annealing the FeNiCrCoCu coating above approximately 600°C will induce nanoscale phase segregation.
The annealing treatment will cause Cu to segregate preferentially to grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary Cu segregation will form discrete nanoscale Cu-rich precipitates.
Sustained temperatures above approximately 600°C provide sufficient atomic diffusion for appreciable nanoscale phase separation in this coating.
Cu-rich grain-boundary precipitates locally increase the coating hardness.
Cu-rich grain-boundary precipitates impede dislocation motion.
Cu-rich grain-boundary precipitates inhibit localized grain-boundary sliding and shear during sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and restricted grain-boundary shear reduce microscopic deformation.
Reduced microscopic deformation decreases material removal and wear.
Under high-temperature sliding, the annealed coating containing Cu-rich precipitates will have lower wear volume than the as-deposited homogeneous coating.
Under high-temperature sliding, the annealed coating will exhibit fewer or narrower localized shear bands than the baseline coating.
At lower temperatures, insufficient diffusion may prevent appreciable precipitate formation and deactivate the proposed mechanism.
Oxidation during high-temperature exposure could alter the observed wear and deformation response.
